tagline: Stage roads and railway towns trace journeys into the Black Hills.
intro: The Wyoming Black Hills Scenic Byway approaches a wooded mountain range rising from the Great Plains. Wyoming’s tourism office describes curves through rock formations and across streams, with dark evergreen-covered hills contrasting with open grassland. It promotes the byway for its historic sites, geology and recreation at the western gateway to the Black Hills.

Travel through this corridor once served the Deadwood goldfields: Four Corners was a stage station on the route connecting them with Cheyenne and the Union Pacific Railroad. Newcastle later developed along the Burlington and Missouri Railroad in the late 1880s. US 16, associated with the Black and Yellow Trail, became a connection between the Black Hills and Yellowstone tourist centers.

For the Newcastle-to-Four Corners portion, begin at Newcastle’s junction of US 16 and US 85, on the southwest edge of the Black Hills. Cambria’s former mining town lies eight miles north of Newcastle, off US 85. Beyond it, Four Corners marks the junction of US 85 and Wyoming 585, southeast of Sundance.

moments.title: Newcastle
moments.text: The Anna Miller Museum occupies a sandstone building made for cavalry horses. Built between 1933 and 1936, the stable was funded by the Civil Works Administration and Works Progress Administration. Its walls are 18 inches thick, using stone quarried on Salt Creek. Plans also called for a riding hall beside it. Workers began the footings, but World War II interrupted the project and the hall was never finished. Stone intended for that hall went into other local construction projects. The Weston County Historical Society has used the stable as the Anna Miller Museum since 1966.

moments.title: Cambria Casino
moments.text: Cambria Casino gives a Wyoming lodge the details of an English Tudor manor. New York architect Bruce Rabenold designed the two-story sandstone building, named for the nearby coal-mining community of Cambria. Part of the property was intended as a memorial to the area’s miners. The dance hall opened in January 1929. Upstairs, the ballroom has a timber-framed roof resembling a medieval hammer-beam truss; those timbers may have come from local mines. The six guest cottages have been removed. The lodge faces a court entered through a gatehouse, with guest-room wings originally flanking the court.

moments.title: Four Corners
moments.text: Four Corners occupies the meeting of US 85 and Wyoming 585 near the Bear Lodge Mountains. Before it was a highway junction, it served as a stage station on the Cheyenne Black Hills Stage Route. That route linked Cheyenne and the Union Pacific Railroad with the goldfields at Deadwood. The community lies north of Newcastle, southeast of Sundance and southwest of Lead, South Dakota.
